name: swapdims_
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::swapdims_(Tensor(a!) self, int dim0, int dim1) -> Tensor(a!). Original Gems pytest owns the full contract — all overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation behavior — and must not be narrowed to this one signature. Registered schemas supplied for this operator (verbatim): aten::swapdims_(Tensor(a!) self, int dim0, int dim1) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics derived from the tests: in-place metadata swap of dims dim0 and dim1 of self. No data is read or moved; only sizes and strides are rewritten, the storage data_ptr and storage_offset stay unchanged, and the caller's own tensor object is returned (res_out is inp). The version-counter delta equals the native aten op's delta in each tested case (the pytest compares deltas, it does not assert an absolute count). Negative dims are normalized against self.dim(); equal dims (e.g. 2,2 or 0,0) and rank-0/rank-1 single-axis cases are no-ops. No operand broadcasting applies; comparisons are exact. The operation is applied to plain, transposed, sliced, offset and stride-0 expanded views, and preserves a conjugate view flag. Out-of-range dims raise IndexError/RuntimeError, non-integer dim arguments (e.g. 0.5, "0") raise RuntimeError/TypeError, and a leaf tensor requiring grad is rejected with RuntimeError. Autograd runs on a non-leaf copy so the gradient reaches the original leaf. Writing through the returned handle is visible in the original tensor.
